section_summary: This section concludes an enclosed coal miners’ policy statement and meeting minutes, then records U.S. occupation correspondence on labor shortages, labor administration, and Japanese labor policy. It includes two copies of a despatch about a meeting with Japanese labor officials, directives on labor supplies and monthly reporting, and the opening page of a despatch conveying industry proposals for labor law changes.

subfiles.title: Coal miners’ policy on shifts and organized activities, conclusion
subfiles.about: The statement proposes shorter coal-mining shifts and a unified campaign for wages, safety, and coal production.
subfiles.summary: Concluding sections call for local combat committees, union unity, six-hour shifts, higher wages, and safety measures.

subfiles.title: Minutes of a Conference of the National Fraction of Coal Miners
subfiles.about: Coal-miner faction members decide how to respond to a split in the Coal Miners Council.
subfiles.summary: The minutes urge propaganda about the split, minimum-wage campaigns, consolidation of remaining unions, and common action with seceding unions. They discuss possible affiliation with the National Congress of Industrial Organizations and separate collective bargaining.

subfiles.title: Department of State charge slip
subfiles.about: A blank form provides fields for charging a document from the file.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 59: Additional Measures to Overcome Labor Shortages
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards an occupation directive seeking further action on shortages of labor for occupation projects.
subfiles.summary: It emphasizes food and clothing distribution and cites restrictions on supplemental rations and excessive payments.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1832/1: Shortage of Japanese Laborers
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.to: Japanese Government, through the Central Liaison Office
subfiles.about: The directive orders further action to address shortages of Japanese laborers.
subfiles.summary: It calls for better food and clothing distribution and progress reports beginning February 10, then every ten days.

subfiles.title: Suggested Decentralization of Administrative Control over Labor Systems and Programs
subfiles.about: The memorandum argues against transferring labor inspection and employment services to Japanese prefectural governments.
subfiles.summary: Holland says central control would better serve labor inspection and employment services. He cites International Labour Organization conventions and asks that this view inform policy discussions on decentralization.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 78: Conversation with Officials of the Japanese Ministry of Labor and Central Labor Committee
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch summarizes a conversation with senior Japanese labor officials and encloses a memorandum of it.
subfiles.summary: Topics include labor efficiency, government staffing, labor-law enforcement, the Emperor’s tours, and fears of disruption by communists and ultra-conservatives.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation with Japanese Labor Officials
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The memorandum records discussion with officials of the Ministry of Labor and Central Labor Committee.
subfiles.summary: The legible portions stress implementing labor legislation, raising worker efficiency, and increasing production despite shortages of raw materials and financing.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 78: Conversation with Officials of the Japanese Ministry of Labor and Central Labor Committee, duplicate copy
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: A second copy of despatch No. 78 summarizes the meeting with Japanese labor officials.
subfiles.summary: It repeats the discussion of worker efficiency, staffing reductions, labor-law enforcement, and political disruption.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation with Japanese Labor Officials, duplicate copy
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: A second copy of the memorandum records the conversation with Japanese labor officials.
subfiles.summary: Its legible passages repeat concerns about workers’ duties, labor efficiency, production, raw materials, and financing.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 98: Submission of Monthly Labor Report by Japanese Government
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards a directive requiring monthly reports on Japanese workers supplied to Allied forces.
subfiles.summary: Reports must show workers supplied, wages paid, and labor services received by Allied organizations.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1852: Submission of Monthly Labor Report
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.to: Japanese Government, through the Central Liaison Office
subfiles.about: The directive specifies monthly prefectural reporting on labor supplied to Allied forces and its cost.
subfiles.summary: For each prefecture, Japan must report requisitioned and procured workers, cash wages, and wages in kind. Figures must be allocated among the listed Allied organizations and countries and submitted monthly.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 95: Comments Regarding the Labor Situation in Japan
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch transmits Japanese industry proposals and a collective-bargaining memorandum concerning labor policy.
subfiles.summary: It reports an Industrial Club study urging removal of communist influence from unions and revisions to labor legislation as measures for economic recovery.
